objective: Register a scenario whose objective reliably drives the planner to emit at least one prohibition-shaped success criterion, and pre-register the paid run that will demonstrate B17-R1's prohibition branch on live input.
evidence: HANDOVER.md §4.2 B17 — OPEN; 'the coverage check cannot read a prohibition'

run readout 2026-09-22 — 'the form branch is demonstrated twice; the inversion, the actual headline fix, still rests on fixtures. A third draw from the same scenario won't reliably reach it'
autornd/graph/checks.py — criteria_addressed shape classification and the prohibition token test

AGENTS.md convention 22 — an instrument's test simulates the condition it watches, end to end
constraints: Free. No paid call, no key, no network. This command builds an input; it does not run anything.
Do NOT modify the coverage check. It is merged and correct. If you believe it is wrong, stop and report — that is a ruling, not a repair.

The scenario is engineered to reach the branch, and the pre-registration MUST say so in its first paragraph. A passing result is then evidence the branch works on live input, not evidence the corpus naturally produces such criteria. Do not let the two be confused.

The objective must name the prohibition explicitly enough that the planner reliably emits a criterion of the form 'avoids the words ...'. State the exact proposed wording in the pre-registration so it can be checked against what the planner actually emitted.

Pre-register four predictions, each numbered: (a) the planner emits at least one prohibition-shaped criterion; (b) coverage classifies it as prohibition, not presence and not form; (c) on a compliant draft, coverage passes; (d) a draft containing a banned token fails. If (d) cannot be reached by this scenario, say so now — do not promise it.

Do not hand-run the scenario to see what it emits. The registration is a file; the run is -027. Predicting and then testing is the structure — if you discover the answer first, the prediction is theatre.
Add a test that the scenario loads and is discoverable by the eval harness, per convention 22.
Do not add a case to the B14 demonstration. B14 is a registered replication of a specific contrast; changing it invalidates its history.
acceptance_criteria: A new scenario is registered under evals/ and loads without a paid call.
A pre-registration file exists under docs/preregistration-*.md, committed, carrying the four numbered predictions and the 'engineered to reach the branch' disclosure in its first paragraph.
The pre-registration's sha is recorded in the response, and it precedes any run.
A test proves the scenario loads and is reachable by the harness.
The coverage check is provably untouched: git diff --stat -- autornd/graph/checks.py is empty.
Suite passes; count reported before and after.

verification.expected: All pass; count reported before and after.
The new scenario loads; the registration is present.
Empty output — neither the check nor the workflow is touched.

rollback: Revert the commit; the scenario is additive and nothing depends on it until -027 runs.
assumptions: The eval harness discovers scenarios by directory convention; the precondition locates that convention before the scenario is written.
The planner's output format can express a prohibition-shaped criterion; if it cannot, that is the finding and -027 does not run.
questions: Should the objective ask for a compliance-shaped deliverable whose failure would be a banned word, or a pure style brief? The first risks the draft actually containing a banned word, which would reach the fail direction (d) but not the pass direction — say which the owner prefers and pre-register that one.
Is there a standing rule that scenarios must not be reverse-engineered from a check's implementation? If so, this scenario violates it in spirit and the owner should say so before it is written.
